first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4%, both pointing to mid-funnel friction. Memory_91 demonstrated that activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action. Memory_31 and memory_86 show that streamlining onboarding improved completion rates and adoption. Rather than respond to competitive pricing pressure with promotional_pricing (memory_73 showed this materially hurt 30-day retention—a false economy), a standard experiment deploying better activation messaging targets the immediate performance gap while preserving long-term retention and sustainable revenue quality. This avoids the retention risk of price-based competition and addresses the measurable activation decline. I'm verifying memory_31 and memory_91 to confirm the magnitude and durability of their effects before scaling.

final.rationale: Archive confirmation strengthens the case: activation_messaging delivered +6% activation lift with +1% retention lift (memory_91), while signup_simplification delivered +9% activation but -1% retention risk (memory_31). Given the 6% QoQ activation decline and 4% onboarding completion decline, activation_messaging is the lower-risk lever that addresses both metrics while protecting retention. Memory_91 showed the effect holds on week-one engagement (+11%) and activation (+6%) without retention drag. Promotional_pricing is ruled out due to memory_73's documented retention damage in the face of competitive pressure. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) targets a different segment. Referral_incentives (memory_57) require established customer base. A standard_experiment on activation_messaging directly targets the observed activation shortfall, leverages proven prior effect, and preserves the long-term revenue quality mandate by avoiding retention trade-offs.
